items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Ken had a recording project later on where he was able to bring in a big band, and we used Loren Schoenberg’s band and we got it done.

ctx.x: What’s it like trying to get your compositions on a recording or get people to play them?

Good question. You know really I’m not a self-promoter I guess. So in that sense I really can’t answer the question. Usually if something of mine has been recorded it’s because they asked me to write it for them in the first place. And even that’s no guarantee. Even I’ve written plenty of things that have not been played yet either for that matter. So, but like the clarinet piece I wrote for Ken Peplowski, that actually started from a draft of a melody that I wrote after a hotel gig and I brought it in when I was…

Boy that’s interesting how things can, little pieces of music can hang around for a while and get changed by circumstances that you wouldn’t conceive of. And it’s worth saving things I guess. And I don’t know about you but I find when I write sometimes I plagiarize myself over and over.

items.q: So eventually James Chirillo and Mark Lopeman and Mike Christiansen arranged... And then he called back and said... I’d like to try the band for ten weeks... And pretty soon found that there were people who do it better than I could... Mark Lopeman and James Chirillo and Mike Christiansen started wr

ctx.x: I was gone. My place was taken by Ted Nash. And I’ll say now, you know, thirty-five years, thirty-four years retrospect, Ted’s a better section player than I am you know. But that was a life lesson, you know what I mean? And then Benny died the following June and I mean I kept doing gigs with the band anyway, when I had gigs, and Benny passed away and then I decided soon after there that this was not going to be a Benny Goodman ghost band. I mean (a) his estate eventually said there will be no ghost band. But I…

that many who you’d want to hear play a Benny Goodman concert, because it would suck. I mean there are a handful, but not that many. And I didn’t know them you know. So I gave that up and then started recording our own albums and we did four or five albums for MusicMasters. And they were nice combinations of, I mean I’m no great arranger. I can arrange — the most arranging I ever did was for Bobby Short during the years when I had his band. But with my own big band, no. I mean I wanted much better writers than…
